**Yes, a 20,000 mAh power bank is allowed on a flight, but only in your carry-on.**

**Why it qualifies**
- The FAA limits lithium-ion power banks to 100 Wh each. The formula is mAh × 3.7 ÷ 1,000, so 20,000 mAh is about 74 Wh, well under the limit ([FAA: Airline Passengers and Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries), [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/best-power-banks-for-flying)).
- Check the Wh rating printed on the unit. If it isn't marked, calculate it from the volts and amp-hours.

**Packing rules**
- Spare batteries and power banks must be in carry-on only, never checked bags ([FAA PackSafe](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)).
- If your carry-on gets gate-checked, take the power bank out and keep it with you in the cabin.
- Protect the terminals from short circuit. Leave it in its retail packaging, or put it in a case or pouch away from loose metal.
- Don't fly with a damaged or recalled unit.

**Airline rules may be stricter than the FAA's.** The FAA says airlines can set tighter limits on quantity and use. Per Dealectric's October 2026 table (a retailer page, so confirm with your airline):
- **Southwest:** one power bank per customer, and you can't charge it from seat power.
- **American and Delta:** two per passenger, and you can't recharge them on board.
- **JetBlue:** two per customer, and you shouldn't use them to power other devices in flight.
- **United:** carry-on only, with no in-flight use rule listed on its page.
- **International carriers:** these can be stricter. Emirates, for example, allows one power bank and no use on board.

Check your airline's page before you fly, especially if you plan to use the power bank in the air. If you tell me which airline you're flying, I can look up its specific policy.

Sources: [FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries), [FAA PackSafe batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7), [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/best-power-banks-for-flying), [IATA](https://www.iata.org/en/youandiata/travelers/batteries/)
